findings.problem: When a name is placed on the left of its stop, the line pill gets drawn between the name and the stop. That pushes the name far away: WORCESTER ends about 955 px from its stop, with the 870 px FRAMINGHAM / WORCESTER LINE pill in between. WICKFORD JUNCTION ends about 590 px away and FORGE PARK/495 about 515 px. Most names on this map sit about 30 px from their dot. These three read as floating labels, which is the 'text confusingly far away' Max said to avoid. The cause is in place_label() in boston-map/src/make_rail_regional.py, lines 805-811. It always draws name, then transfer pills, then line pill, left to right. The score also never charges for the name's own distance from the stop, so the farther left-side spot isn't penalized.
findings.fix: In place_label(), when the chosen side is W, NW or SW, draw the line pill and transfer pills first and the name last. The name then ends one gap from the dot: "[FRAMINGHAM / WORCESTER LINE] WORCESTER o". Another option is to stack the line pill under the name, with both right-aligned to the stop. Also add the name's own distance from its stop to score() (e.g. + own/mpp * a small weight), so a far spot costs more. That would put WORCESTER about 30 px from (1969, 9256), and the same for Forge Park/495 and Wickford Junction.
